title: Molecular Epidemiology, prenatal exposure and prevention of cancer.
ehr_evidence: In the New York City -based “Mothers and Newborns Cohort Study ”, pregnant mothers wore personal air monitors to measure their exposure to PAHs during pregnancy [9].
summary: Review and summary of molecular epidemiology studies on prenatal environmental exposures and their association with biomarkers of cancer risk in a birth cohort.
key_findings: Maternal and cord white blood cells had equivalent levels of PAH-DNA adducts despite the estimated fetal dose being about 10 times lower.
High prenatal PAH exposure was associated with a higher frequency of stable chromosomal aberrations in cord blood.
Global DNA methylation levels in cord blood decreased with increasing prenatal PAH exposure.
Global DNA methylation levels in cord blood were positively correlated with levels of PAH-DNA adducts.
Methylation levels in cord blood and blood collected at age 3 did not vary significantly over time.
captured_features: PAH-DNA adducts in cord and maternal blood
chromosomal aberrations in cord blood lymphocytes
global DNA methylation levels in cord blood
study_design: birth cohort study / molecular epidemiology perspective
data_source_type: birth cohort with biospecimen and environmental monitoring
population: pregnant mothers and newborns in New York City
exposure_domain: prenatal environmental exposures (PAHs, tobacco smoke, pesticides, solvents, radiation, endocrine disruptors)
limitations: measured overall DNA methylation levels rather than specific genes
focus on biomarkers rather than clinical disease outcomes
